ceiling_directive: Prove the full-class incompressible-rigidity inequality, beginning with arbitrary bounded divergence-free periodic C2 maps in the two-node Morse model, and propagate it through the determinant correction to obtain the matching 3/4 upper exponent.
improvement_directive: Resolve oeq:full-incompressible-rigidity affirmatively for the primary two-node C2 Morse class and then extend the argument uniformly over the stated finite-type nuisance classes, replacing the 1/3 full-class upper exponent by 3/4.
critique: The full-class result proves only the wide bracket c epsilon^(3/4) <= Omega(epsilon) <= C epsilon^(1/3) in the primary case, so it does not deliver the sharp full-law modulus named by the project; sharpness is established only for a radial, fixed-mechanism decoder subclass constructed by the note. The general upper bound is a genuine continuity result, but its scalar interpolation argument discards the determinant/incompressible structure and yields a rate too conservative to constitute the advertised frontier. The N^(-1/12) estimator and confidence diameter merely inherit that loose exponent, while the estimator is specified through an existential certified model net and the confidence calibration is stipulated rather than made operational. The synthetic-product identity, exact zero-law identification, localized obstruction, and radial modulus therefore form a worthwhile specialized package, but the load-bearing arbitrary-map rigidity question remains open and keeps the contribution below field tier. The theorem label matching-full-modulus is misleading even though the surrounding prose correctly describes the result as an unmatched bracket. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.7 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
